threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'—locals know there’s only one proper way to travel after dark.
Last week on the 36, someone brought a full chess set. Took up two seats but at least it sparked a game between two strangers. Only in Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a chef's apron juggling bratwursts outside the Kiezkneipe while the tram rumbled past—now that’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can catch a bus that’s just as likely to be delayed by a spontaneous street party as it is by a strike. Classic Berlin!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're local when you can name the coffee shop by the smell wafting from its door, not just the logo on the cup.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing an accordion on the 47 bus, but the real show was a cat in a carrier meowing along. No one batted an eye.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume we all sip on vermut by the hour, but locals really prefer a café con leche and a quick patat de Gràcia on a busy morning.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the 'l' and 'r' in 'Gràcia' – they still say it like it’s a tongue twister.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' and not just 'the overground' when you're getting from Hackney to Dalston.
Spotted a guy on the 59 bus serenading the driver with a ukulele. Driver didn’t even flinch, just kept driving like it was normal.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy hand-rolling his cig on the bench while a toddler danced in the middle of the street - pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand with a line that’s longer than the wait for the U-Bahn, all while locals argue about the best garlic sauce.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name at least three taquerias that used to be something else and point out exactly when the musky smell turned into artisanal coffee.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus yesterday packed with tourists singing 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco.' Only in the TL do you see that kind of tourist charm collide with reality.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about the plazas and bars. They miss the quiet mornings when locals chat over a freshly baked coca in tiny bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at crosswalks, waiting for the green man even when there’s no traffic in sight.
